newsitem.title: BELGIUM: Van Miert demands Italian action on GSM measures.
newsitem.headline: Van Miert demands Italian action on GSM measures.

text.p: European Commissioner Karel Van Miert has called on Italian Prime Minister Romano Prodi to implement measures aimed at creating equal conditions in Italy's digital GSM phone market, Commission sources said.
They said Van Miert had written to Prodi asking him to fix a precise date for the introduction of the changes, which were drawn up by the Commission in October 1995.
The measures were meant to be introduced by the Italian government in January to establish a fair market for Italy's second mobile phone group Omnitel.
Omnitel, an international consortium controlled by Olivetti, launched its GSM mobile phone service in December 1995 to compete with state-controlled Telecom Italia Mobile.
Van Miert complained that Italy had not applied two corrective measures.
The first was a reduction in the connection fees Omnitel has to pay for access to state-controlled telephone lines, which was meant to save the company some 60 billion lire in 1996-97.
The second was legislation designed to allow Omnitel to set up its own telephone infrastructure, giving the firm its own frequencies for radio bridges.
Van Miert was assured by Italian Telecommunications and Post Minister Antonio Maccanico last September that Italy would implement the measures as fast as possible.
The letter complained that Italy's inaction had had "serious consequences" for the GSM sector, the sources said.
